record.original_question: Apply and develop the geometric complexity theory (GCT) representation-theoretic obstruction framework for the variety IMMr,V of small algebraic branching programs.

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Implement the GCT approach to the variety of small algebraic branching programs IMMr,V .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let $r \ge 1$. Consider the space $V^{\otimes d}$ (or, more generally, the affine space of tensors/polynomials computed by width-$r$ algebraic branching programs over $V$). An algebraic branching program (ABP) of width $r$ computing a polynomial $f$ is a directed acyclic layered graph with a source and a sink, in which each edge is labelled by an affine linear form in the variables of $V$ and each internal layer has at most $r$ vertices; the polynomial computed is the sum over source-to-sink paths of the product of the edge labels. Equivalently, width-$r$ ABPs of length $d$ compute the (1,1)-entry of an iterated product $A_1 A_2 \cdots A_d$ of $r \times r$ matrices whose entries are affine linear forms.

Define the variety
$$\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V} \;:=\; \overline{\{\, f \in \mathrm{Sym}^d V^* : f \text{ is computed by some width-}r \text{ ABP over } V\,\}} \;\subseteq\; \mathrm{Sym}^d V^*,$$
where the closure is taken in the Zariski topology. The group $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ acts naturally on $\mathrm{Sym}^d V^*$, and the coordinate ring $\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}]$ decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-modules indexed by partitions $\lambda$, with multiplicities $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$.

A representation-theoretic obstruction to a polynomial $g \in \mathrm{Sym}^d V^*$ lying in $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ is a partition $\lambda$ such that the multiplicity of the irreducible $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-module $S_\lambda V^*$ in the coordinate ring of the $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-orbit closure of $g$ strictly exceeds $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$.

Problem. Develop and carry out the geometric complexity theory (GCT) program for the variety $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$: determine, or give effectively computable bounds on, the multiplicities $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$ for all partitions $\lambda$, and use these to exhibit representation-theoretic obstructions separating explicit polynomial families (such as the permanent or other hard polynomials) from $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ for suitable values of $r$.
artifact.status_search_result: The GCT program for the iterated matrix multiplication / small-width ABP variety remains an active open research direction. Geometric and representation-theoretic properties of IMM have been investigated (e.g. its symmetry group, dual variety, and Jacobian loci), and occurrence obstructions have been studied — with the Occurrence Obstruction Conjecture for permanent vs. determinant having been refuted, in part via results showing that partitions occurring in the IMM coordinate ring also occur for the permanent. However, no full implementation of the GCT obstruction framework for $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ yielding super-polynomial VP vs. VNP-type lower bounds is known.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Aspects of Iterated Matrix Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geometric properties of the IMM polynomial: symmetry group, dual variety, Jacobian loci using representation theory.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric/representation-theoretic study of IMM is ongoing; full GCT obstruction program not completed.

status_evidence.title: No Occurrence Obstructions in Geometric Complexity Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Occurrence Obstruction Conjecture proved false; partitions occurring for IMM also occur for permanent.
status_evidence.claim: A key form of GCT obstruction for IMM has been shown insufficient, indicating the full program for IMM is still open.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to Geometric Complexity Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of GCT program; lower bound goals via multiplicity obstructions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: GCT program for algebraic branching program varieties is acknowledged open.
